intro_text.en: Unit 4 of Engineering Materials Science: the materials a machine uses where strength is not the question. It classifies the non-metals by their bond, follows rubber from latex to a vulcanised compound and shows how an elastomer is chosen for a fluid, treats ceramics from the brick in a furnace wall to the silicon nitride rotor of a turbocharger, works a two-layer refractory wall and an insulator thickness, and ends with the grain, bond and grit of an abrasive and the shear of an adhesive joint. Six solved numericals follow in section 4.6.
intro_text.gu: Engineering Materials Science નું Unit 4: જ્યાં તાકાત પ્રશ્ન નથી ત્યાં મશીન જે સામગ્રી વાપરે છે તે. તે non-metals ને તેમના bond પ્રમાણે વર્ગીકૃત કરે, rubber ને latex થી vulcanised compound સુધી લઈ જાય અને પ્રવાહી પ્રમાણે elastomer કેમ પસંદ થાય તે બતાવે, ceramics ને ભઠ્ઠીની ઈંટ થી turbocharger ના silicon nitride rotor સુધી લઈ જાય, બે સ્તરની refractory દીવાલ અને insulator ની જાડાઈ ગણે, અને abrasive ના grain, bond તથી grit અને adhesive જોડાણના shear પર પૂરું કરે. વિભાગ 4.6 માં છ ઉકેલેલા દાખલા છે.

title.en: 4.1 Non-metallic materials and how they are classified

h.en: Four families, chosen by bond and not by strength
h.gu: ચાર કુટુંબ, તાકાત થી નહીં પણ bond થી નક્કી

body.en:
A non-metallic material is any engineering material that has no free electron sea. That one sentence classifies it: without free electrons there is no metallic bond, so no ductility, no conduction and no weld. The syllabus divides them into four families - polymers (long covalent chains held to each other by weak forces), ceramics (a rigid ionic and covalent network), composites (a stiff fibre carrying the load inside a tough matrix) and natural materials (wood, cork, leather, cotton) which are polymers that grew rather than being made.

Why it is true. the bond fixes everything downstream. A covalent chain with weak forces between the chains gives a low modulus and a low melting point; an ionic network with no free electrons gives hardness, insulation and brittleness; a composite reports the volume-weighted average of a stiff fibre and a tough matrix, which is why its stiffness sits between glass and aluminium.

Common mistake. non-metallic does not mean non-metallic element. Silicon and germanium are elements but they are used as ceramics, and diamond is carbon; rubber is carbon and hydrogen, two non-metals, yet it is an engineering solid with a 22 MPa strength.

Check your answer. before choosing a family, ask the ceiling and the joint. A polymer above 150 C creeps, a ceramic cannot be threaded, and a composite cannot be welded - each one changes the design, not just the material line on the drawing.

h.en: Natural rubber, and what vulcanisation did to it
h.gu: Natural rubber, અને vulcanisation એ શું કર્યું

body.en:
Natural rubber is tapped as latex from the Hevea tree and dried into a gum of cis-1,4 polyisoprene chains. Raw gum is sticky, creeps under its own weight and reaches only about 2 MPa, so for fifty years it was a curiosity rather than an engineering material. In 1839 Goodyear heated it with sulphur and got a rubber that stretches 550 % and comes back: vulcanisation ties neighbouring chains together with sulphur bridges, one every hundred to two hundred chain atoms. The chains can still uncoil - that is the softness - but they can no longer slide past each other, and that is the elasticity.

E = 3G with G = 1.0 MPa -> E = 3.0 MPa (rubber is nearly incompressible) secant modulus at 100 % strain = 1.6/1.0 = 1.6 MPa strain energy to break ~ 0.5 x 22 x 5.5 = 60 MJ per m3 cure: 1 - 3 % sulphur at 140 - 160 C for 10 - 30 min, or a peroxide

Why it is true. a raw chain slides because van der Waals forces between chains are weak. A sulphur bridge is a covalent bond, so it pins two points of two chains together; the length of chain between two bridges still uncoils, which is why cured rubber is soft, but the network cannot flow, which is why the strain returns.

Common mistake. more sulphur is not better. At 30 - 40 % sulphur the same recipe gives ebonite, a hard brittle plastic used for battery boxes and old telephone handsets, not a seal.

h.en: Compounding, and choosing an elastomer for the duty
h.gu: Compounding, અને કામ પ્રમાણે elastomer પસંદ કરવો

body.en:
A rubber part is never one material. The recipe is written in phr - parts per hundred rubber, by weight - and a typical tyre tread is 100 phr natural or SBR, 50 phr carbon black, 3 phr sulphur, 1 phr accelerator, 2 phr zinc oxide and stearic acid, plus an antioxidant and a softener. The carbon black is what turns a 2 MPa gum into a 22 MPa compound: the particles bond to the chains, carry part of the load and stop a crack from running. The choice of base elastomer, though, is decided by the fluid and the temperature, not by the strength.

Why it is true. a seal fails on the fluid long before it fails on the load. Rubber is a polymer network with free volume, so a solvent that wets it diffuses in and swells it; the swelling is a property of the pair, not of the rubber alone, which is why the datasheet prints a volume swell against oil, water and fuel.

Common mistake. a rubber that swells 10 % in service has already failed: a 50 mm O-ring grows to 55 mm, the groove no longer holds it and the joint leaks at the next pressure cycle.

A ceramic is an inorganic solid held by ionic or covalent bonds: alumina (Al2O3), zirconia (ZrO2), silicon carbide (SiC), silicon nitride (Si3N4), porcelain, glass and ordinary brick. The bond is strong and directional, which gives a hardness of 1500 HV and a melting point above 2000 C on a material of density 3.9 g/cm3; the same bond has no free electrons, so it insulates and does not corrode. The price is ductility: alumina carries 2000 MPa in compression and only about 300 MPa in bending, and it does not yield before it breaks.

Why it is true. a metal deforms by moving dislocations; in an ionic lattice a dislocation would bring like charges together, so it cannot move, and the only way left to relieve stress is a crack. One sentence gives both halves of the behaviour - hard, and brittle.

Common mistake. do not design a ceramic for tension or shock. The 2000 MPa compressive figure is real and the 300 MPa bending figure is real, and a tile under a column is safe while the same tile dropped on the floor is not.

h.en: Traditional and advanced ceramics, and where each one goes
h.gu: Traditional અને advanced ceramics, અને દરેક ક્યાં જાય

body.en:
Traditional ceramics are made from clay, feldspar and quartz, shaped wet and fired at 1100 - 1300 C: brick, tile, sanitaryware, porcelain insulators and pottery. Cement and glass belong here too, though one sets by hydration and the other is melted and quenched. Advanced ceramics are chemically pure, sintered from a powder with a controlled grain size, and bought for one property: alumina for wear and insulation, zirconia for toughness by transformation, silicon carbide for thermal shock, silicon nitride for a turbocharger rotor that spins at 100000 rpm.

Why it is true. porosity is what separates the two families. A traditional body is sintered at a temperature low enough to leave 5 - 15 % open pores, which makes it light and insulating; an advanced body is sintered to under 1 % porosity, which makes it strong and is why it costs a hundred times more per kilogram.

Common mistake. firing is not melting. A brick that has been fired has not been liquid, so it keeps its pores; if you design a 10 % shrinkage allowance as if it were a casting, the part comes out undersize in every direction.

h.en: Refractories: the bricks that hold 1500 C

body.en:
A refractory is a ceramic that keeps its shape and its strength in a furnace - above about 1500 C, in contact with slag, flue gas and a heat cycle. Four numbers describe one: its refractoriness (the pyrometric cone equivalent, PCE), its refractoriness under load (RUL, the temperature at which it softens by 0.5 % under 0.2 MPa), its porosity (15 - 25 % in a firebrick) and its resistance to spalling, the cracking that a heat cycle causes. Fireclay is the cheap general brick, silica serves glass tanks, magnesia and dolomite serve steel ladles.

h.en: Insulators: stopping a current and stopping a heat flow are two jobs
h.gu: Insulators: current રોકવો અને ઉષ્મા રોકવી બે જુદાં કામ

An electrical insulator is judged by its dielectric strength, in kV per mm, and by its resistivity; a thermal insulator is judged by its conductivity, in W/m K, and the two lists hardly overlap. Porcelain, glass, epoxy, bakelite, PTFE and dry transformer oil stop current; glass wool, rock wool, thermocol, ceramic fibre and aerogel stop heat. The best insulator of all is a still gas - air is 0.026 W/m K and 3 kV/mm - which is why foams, wools and aerogels are mostly trapped air.

h.en: Abrasives: the grain, the bond and the grit number
h.gu: Abrasives: grain, bond અને grit number

body.en:
An abrasive is a material harder than the work it has to cut. The natural ones are sandstone, emery (60 - 70 % alumina in iron oxide), corundum and diamond; almost everything sold today is synthetic - silicon carbide, made in an electric furnace since 1891, fused alumina, cubic boron nitride since 1957 and synthetic diamond. The grain is held in a bond - vitrified clay for a bench wheel, resinoid for a cut-off disc, rubber and shellac for a polishing wheel, paper or cloth for a coated belt - and it is sized by a grit number: 8 - 24 coarse, 30 - 60 medium, 80 - 180 fine, 220 - 600 for lapping.

h.en: Adhesives: the joint is the design

body.en:
An adhesive joins two parts through surface attraction instead of a rivet or a weld. Structural adhesives - epoxy, toughened acrylic, polyurethane - carry real load; cyanoacrylate and hot melt are for small or temporary work; anaerobic grades lock a thread. The glue is only half the joint: the surface must be degreased, abraded to 0.5 - 2 um and often primed, because adhesion happens in the first few molecular layers. A lap joint loaded in shear over the largest area is strong; the same glue in peel is ten times weaker.

h.en: An alumina spacer that cannot expand

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

An alumina spacer of E 300 GPa and alpha 8.0e-6 per K is clamped between steel flanges so that it cannot expand. Find the stress in the spacer at a temperature rise of 200 K and of 100 K, compare with its 300 MPa flexural strength, and state two ways to make the joint safe.

Step 1 - the constrained stress

sigma = E alpha dT = 300e9 x 8.0e-6 x dT = 2.4e6 x dT Pa dT = 200 K: sigma = 2.4e6 x 200 = 480 MPa dT = 100 K: sigma = 2.4e6 x 100 = 240 MPa

Step 2 - compare with the strength

flexural strength 300 MPa 480/300 = 1.60 -> the spacer is 60 % over its strength and cracks 240/300 = 0.80 -> factor of safety 1.25, thin but safe
480 MPa at 200 K is a cracked spacer; 240 MPa at 100 K is a marginal one

Step 3 - two ways to make the joint safe

1. leave a clearance of alpha L dT, or put a compliant gasket in the joint 2. use fused silica instead: 72e9 x 0.55e-6 x 200 = 7.9 MPa

A fully constrained ceramic is the worst case in the whole of Unit 4: the metal frame has a higher expansion coefficient and a much higher strength, so it wins the argument and the ceramic breaks. Either let the ceramic move, or soften the load path with a gasket, or choose a ceramic with a lower expansion coefficient - fused silica at 0.55e-6 develops only 7.9 MPa where alumina develops 480 MPa.

Check your answer. Units: E in Pa and alpha in per K give a stress in Pa, so 2.4e6 x 200 = 480e6 Pa = 480 MPa. Check the sign too: on cooling the stress reverses, and a ceramic is just as weak in tension then.

પ્રશ્ન (7 marks)

E 300 GPa અને alpha 8.0e-6 પ્રતિ K નું alumina spacer steel flange વચ્ચે એવી રીતે clamp થયું છે કે ફેલાઈ શકે નહીં. 200 K અને 100 K તાપમાન વધારા પર spacer માં stress શોધો, તેની 300 MPa flexural strength સાથે સરખાવો, અને જોડાણ સલામત કરવાની બે રીતો કહો.

પગલું 1 - રોકાયેલો stress

sigma = E alpha dT = 300e9 x 8.0e-6 x dT = 2.4e6 x dT Pa dT = 200 K: sigma = 2.4e6 x 200 = 480 MPa dT = 100 K: sigma = 2.4e6 x 100 = 240 MPa

પગલું 2 - તાકાત સાથે સરખામણી

flexural strength 300 MPa 480/300 = 1.60 -> the spacer is 60 % over its strength and cracks 240/300 = 0.80 -> factor of safety 1.25, thin but safe
480 MPa at 200 K is a cracked spacer; 240 MPa at 100 K is a marginal one

પગલું 3 - જોડાણ સલામત કરવાની બે રીતો

1. leave a clearance of alpha L dT, or put a compliant gasket in the joint 2. use fused silica instead: 72e9 x 0.55e-6 x 200 = 7.9 MPa

આખા Unit 4 માં fully constrained ceramic સૌથી ખરાબ કિસ્સો છે: metal frame નું expansion coefficient વધારે અને તાકાત ઘણી વધારે હોય, તેથી તે જીતે અને ceramic તૂટે. Ceramic ને ખસવા દો, અથવા gasket થી લોડનો રસ્તો નરમ કરો, અથવા ઓછા expansion વાળું ceramic પસંદ કરો - fused silica 0.55e-6 પર ફક્ત 7.9 MPa બનાવે જ્યાં alumina 480 MPa બનાવે.

જવાબ ચકાસો. એકમ: Pa માં E અને પ્રતિ K માં alpha એટલે Pa માં stress, તેથી 2.4e6 x 200 = 480e6 Pa = 480 MPa. ચિહ્ન પણ ચકાસો: ઠંડા પડતાં stress ઊલટો થાય, અને ceramic ત્યારે પણ તેટલું જ નબળું છે.

Question (6 marks)

Compare the thermal shock resistance of alumina (300 MPa, nu 0.22, E 300 GPa, alpha 8.0e-6), soda-lime glass (50 MPa, nu 0.22, E 70 GPa, alpha 9.0e-6) and fused silica (110 MPa, nu 0.17, E 72 GPa, alpha 0.55e-6). Say which one can be quenched in water and why.

Step 1 - the parameter R

R = sigma_f (1 - nu)/(E alpha), the temperature step the part survives alumina: 300e6 x 0.78/(300e9 x 8.0e-6) = 234e6/2.4e6 = 97 K soda glass: 50e6 x 0.78/(70e9 x 9.0e-6) = 39e6/0.63e6 = 62 K fused silica: 110e6 x 0.83/(72e9 x 0.55e-6) = 91.3e6/39.6e3 = 2305 K

Step 2 - what the numbers mean

a hot alumina part dropped in water sees about 200 K, so it cracks a glass part cracks at 62 K, so it cracks in warm water silica at 2305 K survives any quench a workshop can give it
alumina 97 K, soda-lime glass 62 K, fused silica 2305 K

Fused silica is 24 times tougher against a quench than alumina, and it gets there not by being strong but by having almost no expansion: alpha 0.55e-6 against 8.0e-6 cancels the strength difference completely. That is why a laboratory crucible is silica and not alumina, and why a glass-ceramic cooktop can take a hot pan while ordinary window glass cannot.

Check your answer. R has the unit of temperature - if your answer comes out in MPa or in kelvin per metre, the bracket was assembled wrongly.

h.en: A furnace wall, and what the insulation saves
h.gu: ભઠ્ઠીની દીવાલ, અને insulation શું બચાવે

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

A furnace wall is 230 mm of firebrick (k 1.0 W/m K) on the hot side and 115 mm of insulating brick (k 0.12 W/m K) outside it. The hot face is at 1200 C and the cold face at 50 C. Find the heat loss per m2, the interface temperature, and the money saved per m2 in a month if the furnace runs continuously at Rs 8 per kWh.

Step 1 - the two resistances

R1 = 0.230/1.00 = 0.230 m2 K/W R2 = 0.115/0.12 = 0.958 m2 K/W sum = 1.188 m2 K/W

Step 2 - the heat flux and the interface

q = (1200 - 50)/1.188 = 968 W per m2 T(interface) = 1200 - 968 x 0.230 = 1200 - 223 = 977 C check from the cold side: 50 + 968 x 0.958 = 977 C

Step 3 - what the insulation saves

bare firebrick: q = 1150/0.230 = 5000 W per m2 saving = 5000 - 968 = 4032 W per m2 = 4.03 kW per m2 one month = 720 h: 4.03 x 720 = 2903 kWh; at Rs 8 = Rs 23,224 per m2
968 W per m2, 977 C at the joint, Rs 23,224 per m2 per month saved

The insulation is 115 mm thick against 230 mm of firebrick, and it takes 81 % of the temperature drop. That is the point of a two-layer wall: the cheap dense brick is there to resist the slag and the abrasion, and the thin, more expensive insulating layer is there to do the saving.

Check your answer. The flux must be the same through both layers - if your two interface temperatures differ, one of the resistances is wrong.

પ્રશ્ન (7 marks)

ભઠ્ઠીની દીવાલ ગરમ બાજુ 230 mm firebrick (k 1.0 W/m K) અને બહાર 115 mm insulating brick (k 0.12 W/m K) ની છે. ગરમ સપાટી 1200 C અને ઠંડી સપાટી 50 C છે. પ્રતિ m2 ઉષ્માનો વ્યય, interface નું તાપમાન, અને ભઠ્ઠી સતત ચાલે તો Rs 8 પ્રતિ kWh પર એક મહિનામાં પ્રતિ m2 કેટલા રૂપિયા બચે તે શોધો.

પગલું 1 - બે resistance

R1 = 0.230/1.00 = 0.230 m2 K/W R2 = 0.115/0.12 = 0.958 m2 K/W sum = 1.188 m2 K/W

પગલું 2 - heat flux અને interface

q = (1200 - 50)/1.188 = 968 W per m2 T(interface) = 1200 - 968 x 0.230 = 1200 - 223 = 977 C check from the cold side: 50 + 968 x 0.958 = 977 C

પગલું 3 - insulation શું બચાવે

bare firebrick: q = 1150/0.230 = 5000 W per m2 saving = 5000 - 968 = 4032 W per m2 = 4.03 kW per m2 one month = 720 h: 4.03 x 720 = 2903 kWh; at Rs 8 = Rs 23,224 per m2
968 W per m2, 977 C at the joint, Rs 23,224 per m2 per month saved

Insulation 230 mm firebrick સામે 115 mm જ જાડું છે, અને તાપમાનનો 81 % ઘટાડો લે છે. બે સ્તરની દીવાલનો આ જ મુદ્દો છે: સસ્તી ગાઢ ઈંટ slag અને ઘસારો ઝીલવા, અને પાતળું મોંઘું અવાહક સ્તર બચત કરવા.

જવાબ ચકાસો. બંને સ્તરમાંથી flux એક જ આવવો જોઈએ - બંને બાજુનું interface તાપમાન જુદું આવે તો એક resistance ખોટો છે.

h.en: Porosity and absorption of a firebrick

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

A firebrick sample of bulk volume 120 cm3 weighs 320 g dry and 345 g after soaking in water. Find its bulk density, its water absorption, its apparent porosity and its true density, and say what that porosity does to the brick.

Step 1 - the water that went in

water absorbed = 345 - 320 = 25 g, so 25 cm3 of open pore

Step 2 - the four numbers

bulk density = 320/120 = 2.67 g/cm3 water absorption = 25/320 x 100 = 7.8 % apparent porosity = 25/120 x 100 = 20.8 % true density = 320/(120 - 25) = 3.37 g/cm3
2.67 g/cm3 bulk, 20.8 % open pore, 7.8 % absorption, 3.37 g/cm3 true

One brick in five is empty space. That is why a firebrick insulates so well - the pores hold still air at 0.026 W/m K - and it is also why its cold crushing strength is 20 to 60 MPa against 3000 MPa for a dense alumina. Porosity buys insulation and pays for it in strength and in slag penetration, because the same open pores that let water in let slag in as well.

Check your answer. The two porosity routes must agree: 1 - 2.67/3.37 = 20.8 %, the same as 25/120.

પ્રશ્ન (6 marks)

120 cm3 bulk volume નો firebrick નમૂનો સૂકો 320 g અને પાણીમાં પલાળ્યા પછી 345 g છે. તેની bulk density, water absorption, apparent porosity અને true density શોધો, અને એ porosity ઈંટ સાથે શું કરે તે કહો.

પગલું 1 - અંદર ગયેલું પાણી

water absorbed = 345 - 320 = 25 g, so 25 cm3 of open pore

પગલું 2 - ચાર આંકડા

bulk density = 320/120 = 2.67 g/cm3 water absorption = 25/320 x 100 = 7.8 % apparent porosity = 25/120 x 100 = 20.8 % true density = 320/(120 - 25) = 3.37 g/cm3
2.67 g/cm3 bulk, 20.8 % open pore, 7.8 % absorption, 3.37 g/cm3 true

ઈંટનો પાંચમો ભાગ ખાલી જગ્યા છે. તેથી જ firebrick એટલી સારી રીતે અવાહક છે - છિદ્રોમાં સ્થિર હવા 0.026 W/m K પર રહે - અને તેથી જ તેની cold crushing strength 20 થી 60 MPa છે જ્યારે ગાઢ alumina ની 3000 MPa. Porosity insulation ખરીદે અને તેની કિંમત તાકાત તથી slag ઘૂસવામાં ચૂકવે, કારણ કે જે છિદ્રોમાં પાણી ગયું તેમાં slag પણ જાય.

જવાબ ચકાસો. Porosity ના બંને રસ્તા મળવા જોઈએ: 1 - 2.67/3.37 = 20.8 %, જે 25/120 જ છે.

h.en: An adhesive lap joint, and its factor of safety
h.gu: Adhesive lap joint, અને તેનું factor of safety

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

A bracket is glued to a plate with an epoxy whose lap shear strength is 20 MPa. The overlap is 25 mm wide and 40 mm long and the working load is 5 kN. Find the shear stress in the joint, its factor of safety, and the greatest load it may carry at a required factor of safety of 3.

Step 1 - the shear stress

A = 25 x 40 = 1000 mm2 tau = P/A = 5000/1000 = 5.0 MPa

Step 2 - the factor of safety

SF = 20/5.0 = 4.0

Step 3 - the load allowed at SF 3

tau_allow = 20/3 = 6.67 MPa P_max = 6.67 x 1000 = 6667 N = 6.67 kN
5.0 MPa working, factor of safety 4.0, 6.67 kN at a factor of 3

The joint is comfortable in shear, and that is the only reason it works. The same bracket in peel would carry a small fraction of 20 kN, because peel loads one adhesive line at a time instead of the whole area. A designer who wants the strength of the glue has to give it area in shear and keep the prying load out.

Check your answer. Bond line thickness is not in this sum, but it decides the answer in practice: 0.1 - 0.2 mm is right, and a thick brittle line cracks before the sum says it should.

tau_allow = 20/3 = 6.67 MPa P_max = 6.67 x 1000 = 6667 N = 6.67 kN
5.0 MPa working, factor of safety 4.0, 6.67 kN at a factor of 3

જોડાણ shear માં આરામદાયક છે, અને એ જ એક કારણે ચાલે છે. એ જ bracket peel માં 20 kN નો થોડો ભાગ જ ઉપાડે, કારણ કે peel આખા area ને બદલે એક વખતે એક adhesive લાઇન પર લોડ નાખે. ગુંદરની તાકાત જોઈએ તો designer એ shear માં area આપવો પડે અને ઉચકવાનો લોડ દૂર રાખવો પડે.

જવાબ ચકાસો. Bond line ની જાડાઈ આ ગણતરીમાં નથી, પણ વ્યવહારમાં જવાબ એ જ નક્કી કરે: 0.1 - 0.2 mm સાચું છે, અને જાડી ભંગુર લાઇન ગણતરી કહે તે પહેલાં તૂટે.

h.en: How thick must the insulator be

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

A bakelite support of dielectric strength 18 kV/mm is used on an 11 kV busbar. For a 3 mm sheet, find the breakdown voltage and the factor of safety at 11 kV; then find the least thickness that gives a factor of safety of 3, and say why the surface path is checked separately.

Step 1 - the breakdown of the sheet

V_break = E_b x d = 18 x 3 = 54 kV

Step 2 - the factor of safety on 11 kV

SF = 54/11 = 4.9

Step 3 - the thickness for a factor of 3

required withstand = 3 x 11 = 33 kV t = V/E_b = 33/18 = 1.83 mm, so 2 mm is specified and 3 mm is comfortable
54 kV breakdown, factor 4.9 at 11 kV, 1.83 mm needed for a factor of 3

Thickness stops a puncture and nothing else. The flashover travels over the surface, so it is stopped by distance - the creepage length - and a wet or dusty surface has a far lower flashover voltage than a clean one. That is why a 3 mm sheet of bakelite on a 11 kV busbar is wrapped in a long ribbed porcelain or epoxy shed rather than left bare.

Check your answer. Keep kV and mm together: 18 kV/mm times 3 mm is 54 kV, and never multiply by a factor of safety twice - once in the thickness and once in the load.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (6 marks)

18 kV/mm dielectric strength વાળું bakelite support 11 kV busbar પર વપરાય છે. 3 mm sheet માટે breakdown વોલ્ટેજ અને 11 kV પર factor of safety શોધો; પછી factor of safety 3 આપતી ઓછામાં ઓછી જાડાઈ શોધો, અને સપાટીનો રસ્તો અલગ કેમ ચકાસાય તે કહો.

પગલું 1 - sheet નું breakdown

V_break = E_b x d = 18 x 3 = 54 kV

પગલું 2 - 11 kV પર factor of safety

SF = 54/11 = 4.9

પગલું 3 - factor 3 માટે જાડાઈ

required withstand = 3 x 11 = 33 kV t = V/E_b = 33/18 = 1.83 mm, so 2 mm is specified and 3 mm is comfortable
54 kV breakdown, factor 4.9 at 11 kV, 1.83 mm needed for a factor of 3

જાડાઈ ફક્ત puncture રોકે. Flashover સપાટી પર થી પસાર થાય, તેથી તે અંતર - creepage લંબાઈ - થી રોકાય, અને ભીની કે ધૂળવાળી સપાટીનું flashover વોલ્ટેજ સાફ કરતાં ઘણું નીચું હોય. તેથી 11 kV busbar પરનું 3 mm bakelite નગ્ન નહીં, લાંબી ribbed porcelain કે epoxy છત્રીમાં લપેટાય.

જવાબ ચકાસો. kV અને mm સાથે રાખો: 18 kV/mm ગુણ્યા 3 mm એટલે 54 kV, અને factor of safety બે વાર ન લગાવો - એક વાર જાડાઈમાં અને ફરી લોડમાં નહીં.

caption.en: Polymers, ceramics, composites and natural materials: four families that a mechanical drawing uses for weight, insulation, quiet running and cost, not for strength.
caption.gu: Polymers, ceramics, composites અને natural materials: ચાર કુટુંબ જે ડ્રોઇંગ વજન, અવાહકતા, શાંત ચાલ અને ભાવ માટે વાપરે, તાકાત માટે નહીં.

caption.en: Sulphur bridges turn a soft gum that stretches and stays stretched into a rubber that returns; the same 500 % elongation now comes back to zero.
caption.gu: Sulphur ના પુલ નરમ gum ને, જે ખેંચાઈને ખેંચાયેલું જ રહે, એવા rubber માં ફેરવે જે પાછું આવે; એ જ 500 % elongation હવે શૂન્ય પર પાછું આવે.

title.gu: દરેક કુટુંબ કેટલી ગરમી સુધી ચાલે

caption.en: The ceiling on service temperature runs with the bond: van der Waals forces in a polymer, metallic bonds in a metal, ionic and covalent bonds in a ceramic.
caption.gu: સેવાનું તાપમાન bond પ્રમાણે ચાલે: polymer માં van der Waals બળ, metal માં metallic bond, ceramic માં ionic અને covalent bond.

title.gu: Metal, ceramic અને polymer ની સરખામણી

caption.en: Bond, strength, ductility, ceiling, density and failure mode - six questions asked of all three families, so a choice is made from properties and not from habit.
caption.gu: Bond, તાકાત, ductility, મર્યાદા, density અને તૂટવાની રીત - ત્રણેય કુટુંબને પૂછાતા છ પ્રશ્નો, જેથી પસંદગી ટેવ પ્રમાણે નહીં ગુણધર્મ પ્રમાણે થાય.

caption.en: 1200 C at the hot face and 50 C at the shell, with 977 C at the joint: the firebrick carries most of the temperature drop and the thin insulation layer saves 80 % of the heat.
caption.gu: ગરમ સપાટી પર 1200 C અને shell પર 50 C, જોડાણ પર 977 C: મોટો તાપમાન ઘટાડો firebrick લે છે અને પાતળું અવાહક સ્તર 80 % ઉષ્મા બચાવે છે.

caption.en: Dielectric strength decides the thickness: air is 3 kV/mm and PTFE is 24, so the same busbar needs a very different wall around it.
caption.gu: જાડાઈ dielectric strength નક્કી કરે: હવા 3 kV/mm અને PTFE 24, તેથી એક જ busbar ને સાવ જુદી દીવાલ જોઈએ.

title.en: The Mohs ladder and the abrasives

caption.en: Quartz at 7, corundum at 9 and diamond at 10 on the Mohs scale, and the synthetic abrasives placed between them by Knoop hardness.
caption.gu: Mohs પર quartz 7, corundum 9 અને diamond 10, અને synthetic abrasives Knoop hardness થી તેમની વચ્ચે ગોઠવાય છે.

terms.en: Rubber is nearly incompressible, so its tensile modulus is three times the shear modulus: G 1.0 MPa gives E 3.0 MPa.
terms.gu: Rubber લગભગ incompressible છે, તેથી tensile modulus shear modulus ના ત્રણ ગણું: G 1.0 MPa એટલે E 3.0 MPa.

items.f: sigma = E eps   (secant: sigma/eps at that strain)

terms.en: Rubber softens as it stretches, so the secant modulus is quoted at 100 % strain rather than at 1 %.
terms.gu: Rubber ખેંચાતાં નરમ પડે, તેથી secant modulus 1 % નહીં 100 % strain પર આપાય.

items.f: W = 0.5 sigma eps   (area under the curve)

terms.en: 22 MPa at 550 % gives about 60 MJ per m3, which is why a rubber bumper absorbs a blow that would dent steel.
terms.gu: 550 % પર 22 MPa એટલે લગભગ 60 MJ પ્રતિ m3, તેથી rubber bumper એવો ધક્કો શોષે જે સ્ટીલને ખાડો પાડે.

terms.en: A part that cannot expand develops this stress; alumina at 200 K gives 480 MPa against a 300 MPa strength.
terms.gu: જે ભાગ ફેલાઈ શકે નહીં તેમાં આ stress બને; 200 K પર alumina 300 MPa તાકાત સામે 480 MPa આપે.

terms.en: The temperature step a brittle material survives: 97 K for alumina, 2300 K for fused silica, which is why silica crucibles can be quenched.
terms.gu: ભંગુર સામગ્રી જે તાપમાનનો ફટકો ઝીલે: alumina માટે 97 K, fused silica માટે 2300 K, તેથી silica crucible ઠારી શકાય.

terms.en: Strength falls as the square root of the flaw size: 50 um gives 276 MPa and 200 um gives 138 MPa in the same alumina.
terms.gu: તિરાડના માપના વર્ગમૂળ પ્રમાણે તાકાત ઘટે: એ જ alumina માં 50 um એટલે 276 MPa અને 200 um એટલે 138 MPa.

terms.en: Steady one-dimensional flow: 1200 C to 50 C across 0.230 m of firebrick and 0.115 m of insulation is 968 W per m2.
terms.gu: સ્થિર એક-દિશા પ્રવાહ: 0.230 m firebrick અને 0.115 m insulation પાર 1200 C થી 50 C એટલે 968 W પ્રતિ m2.

terms.en: Adds in series like an electrical resistance: 0.230 and 0.958 m2 K/W here.
terms.gu: Electrical resistance ની જેમ series માં જોડાય: અહીં 0.230 અને 0.958 m2 K/W.

terms.en: Gives the interface temperature: 1200 - 968 x 0.230 = 977 C.
terms.gu: Interface નું તાપમાન આપે: 1200 - 968 x 0.230 = 977 C.

terms.en: Breakdown voltage per millimetre: air 3, porcelain 15, PTFE 24 kV/mm.
terms.gu: પ્રતિ મિલીમીટર breakdown વોલ્ટેજ: હવા 3, porcelain 15, PTFE 24 kV/mm.

terms.en: 11 kV with a factor of 3 in porcelain: 33/15 = 2.2 mm, so 3 mm is specified.
terms.gu: Porcelain માં factor 3 સાથે 11 kV: 33/15 = 2.2 mm, તેથી 3 mm લખાય.

terms.en: 50 mm of glass wool at 0.040 W/m K over 10 K loses 8 W per m2.
terms.gu: 0.040 W/m K નું 50 mm glass wool 10 K પર 8 W પ્રતિ m2 ગુમાવે.

terms.en: 250 mm at 2000 rpm is 26 m/s; a vitrified wheel is rated 35 m/s.
terms.gu: 250 mm પર 2000 rpm એટલે 26 m/s; vitrified wheel 35 m/s સુધી રેટેડ છે.

terms.en: 5 kN over 25 x 40 mm is 5 MPa, against 20 MPa for epoxy.
terms.gu: 25 x 40 mm પર 5 kN એટલે 5 MPa, epoxy ના 20 MPa સામે.

name.en: Factor of safety of a joint

terms.en: 20/5 = 4 here; a design that asks for 3 carries 6.67 kN instead of 5 kN.
terms.gu: અહીં 20/5 = 4; 3 માંગતું design 5 kN ને બદલે 6.67 kN ઉપાડે.

a.en: Any engineering material with no free electron sea. The syllabus groups it into polymers, ceramics, composites and natural materials, and the bond - not the strength - is what separates them.
a.gu: Free electrons નો સમુદ્ર ન હોય તેવી કોઈ પણ ઇજનેરી સામગ્રી. Syllabus તેને polymers, ceramics, composites અને natural materials માં વહેંચે છે, અને તાકાત નહીં, bond તેમને જુદા પાડે છે.

q.en: Why does a machine need a non-metal at all?
q.gu: મશીનને non-metal ની જરૂર કેમ પડે?

a.en: For weight, insulation, quiet running and corrosion resistance: a guard, a tank liner, a cable insulator, a rubber mount and a cork gasket are all jobs a metal does badly or expensively.
a.gu: વજન, insulation, શાંત ચાલ અને કાટ સામે ટકવા માટે: guard, ટાંકીનું lining, cable insulator, rubber mount અને cork gasket - આ બધું metal મોંઘું કે ખરાબ કરે.

q.en: What is a composite, and why is it used?
q.gu: Composite એટલે શું, અને કેમ વપરાય?

a.en: A stiff fibre inside a tough matrix - glass or carbon in epoxy, silicon carbide in aluminium. The fibre carries the load and the matrix spreads it, so the stiffness per kilogram is three to four times that of steel.
a.gu: લચીલા matrix માં કઠણ fibre - epoxy માં glass કે carbon, aluminium માં silicon carbide. Fibre લોડ ઉપાડે અને matrix ફેલાવે, તેથી કિલો દીઠ કઠણાઈ સ્ટીલ કરતાં ત્રણ-ચાર ગણી.

q.en: What is vulcanisation and what does it change?
q.gu: Vulcanisation એટલે શું અને શું બદલે?

a.en: Heating rubber with 1 - 3 % sulphur so that sulphur bridges form between chains. The strength rises from 2 to 22 MPa and the strain of 550 % becomes recoverable - the gum becomes an elastic solid.
a.gu: 1 - 3 % sulphur સાથે rubber ગરમ કરવું જેથી chains વચ્ચે sulphur પુલ બને. તાકાત 2 થી 22 MPa થાય અને 550 % strain પાછું આવે - gum લચીલો ઘન બને.

q.en: Why is carbon black added to a rubber compound?
q.gu: Rubber compound માં carbon black કેમ ઉમેરાય?

a.en: It bonds to the chains, carries part of the load and blunts a running crack. 50 phr of black takes the tensile strength from 2 to 22 MPa and the 100 % modulus from 1.6 to 4.5 MPa.
a.gu: તે chains સાથે જોડાય, લોડનો ભાગ ઉપાડે અને દોડતી તિરાડ અટકાવે. 50 phr black tensile strength 2 થી 22 MPa અને 100 % modulus 1.6 થી 4.5 MPa કરે.

q.en: Why is nitrile rubber used for an oil seal and not natural rubber?
q.gu: તેલના seal માટે natural rubber નહીં, nitrile કેમ?

a.en: Because swell is a property of the rubber-fluid pair: natural rubber takes up 50 % in mineral oil and nitrile only about 5 %. A swollen seal loses its grip in the groove and leaks.
a.gu: કારણ કે ફૂલવું એ rubber અને પ્રવાહીની જોડીનું ગુણધર્મ છે: natural rubber ખનીજ તેલમાં 50 % લે, nitrile ફક્ત 5 %. ફૂલેલો seal groove માં પકડ ગુમાવે અને ચૂ થાય.

q.en: Why is a ceramic hard and brittle at the same time?
q.gu: Ceramic સખત અને ભંગુર એક સાથે કેમ?

a.en: Because a dislocation cannot move through a rigid ionic lattice - it would bring like charges together - so the material cannot yield, and the only way to relieve stress is a crack. Hardness and brittleness are the same fact.
a.gu: કારણ કે કઠણ ionic lattice માં dislocation ખસી શકે નહીં - સરખા charge પાસે આવે - તેથી સામગ્રી yield થઈ શકે નહીં, અને stress ઓછો કરવાનો એક જ રસ્તો તિરાડ છે. સખતાઈ અને ભંગુરતા એક જ હકીકત છે.

q.en: What separates a traditional ceramic from an advanced one?
q.gu: Traditional અને advanced ceramic માં શું ફરક?

a.en: Purity, porosity and price: a traditional body is fired with 5 - 15 % open pores and costs a few rupees a kilogram; an advanced body is sintered below 1 % porosity for one property and costs a hundred times more.
a.gu: શુદ્ધતા, porosity અને ભાવ: traditional body 5 - 15 % ખુલ્લા છિદ્ર સાથે પાકે અને કિલો થોડા રૂપિયા; advanced body એક ગુણધર્મ માટે 1 % થી ઓછા porosity સુધી sinter થાય અને સો ગણું મોંઘું પડે.

q.en: What is an acidic and a basic refractory, and why match the slag?
q.gu: Acidic અને basic refractory એટલે શું, અને slag કેમ મેળવવો?

a.en: Silica is acidic and magnesia or dolomite is basic; a basic slag dissolves an acid brick. Chromite and graphite are neutral and survive either slag, which is why they are used where the charge changes.
a.gu: Silica acidic છે અને magnesia કે dolomite basic; basic slag acidic ઈંટને ઓગાળે. Chromite અને graphite neutral છે અને બંને slag ઝીલે, તેથી જ્યાં charge બદલાય ત્યાં વપરાય.

q.en: How do you decide the thickness of an insulator?
q.gu: Insulator ની જાડાઈ કેમ નક્કી કરો?

a.en: Divide the withstand voltage by the dielectric strength: t = V x SF/E_b. For 11 kV and a factor of 3 in porcelain, 33/15 gives 2.2 mm, so 3 mm is drawn. The surface leakage path is checked separately.
a.gu: Withstand વોલ્ટેજને dielectric strength થી ભાગો: t = V x SF/E_b. Porcelain માં 11 kV અને factor 3 માટે 33/15 એટલે 2.2 mm, તેથી 3 mm લખાય. સપાટીનો leakage પથ અલગ ચકાસાય.

q.en: What is self-sharpening of a grinding wheel?
q.gu: Grinding wheel નું self-sharpening એટલે શું?

a.en: As the grain dulls, the cutting force on it rises until the bond breaks and the worn grain falls out, leaving a fresh edge. The bond is therefore chosen for the work: hard bond on soft material, soft bond on hard material.
a.gu: Grain થૂંસાતાં તેના પરનું કાપવાનું બળ વધે, bond તૂટે અને ઘસાયેલો grain નીકળી જાય, નવી ધાર મળે. તેથી bond કામ પ્રમાણે પસંદ થાય: નરમ સામગ્રી પર સખત bond, સખત પર નરમ.

q.en: Why is a lap joint stronger than a butt joint?
q.gu: Lap joint butt joint કરતાં મજબૂત કેમ?

a.en: Because the load is carried in shear over the overlap area instead of in peel at an edge. A butt joint on a 20 MPa epoxy carries less than a lap joint on a 6 MPa PVA, so the geometry matters more than the glue.
a.gu: કારણ કે લોડ ધાર પર peel માં નહીં, overlap area પર shear માં ઉપડે. 20 MPa epoxy નું butt joint 6 MPa PVA ના lap joint કરતાં ઓછું ઉપાડે, તેથી ગુંદર કરતાં ભૂમિતિ વધુ મહત્વની.

q.en: An alumina spacer of E 300 GPa and alpha 8.0e-6 per K is clamped between steel flanges so that it cannot expand. Find the stress in the spacer at a temperature rise of 200 K and of 100 K, compare with its 300 MPa flexural strength, and state two ways to make the joint safe.
q.gu: E 300 GPa અને alpha 8.0e-6 પ્રતિ K નું alumina spacer steel flange વચ્ચે એવી રીતે clamp થયું છે કે ફેલાઈ શકે નહીં. 200 K અને 100 K તાપમાન વધારા પર spacer માં stress શોધો, તેની 300 MPa flexural strength સાથે સરખાવો, અને જોડાણ સલામત કરવાની બે રીતો કહો.

q.en: Compare the thermal shock resistance of alumina (300 MPa, nu 0.22, E 300 GPa, alpha 8.0e-6), soda-lime glass (50 MPa, nu 0.22, E 70 GPa, alpha 9.0e-6) and fused silica (110 MPa, nu 0.17, E 72 GPa, alpha 0.55e-6). Say which one can be quenched in water and why.
q.gu: Alumina (300 MPa, nu 0.22, E 300 GPa, alpha 8.0e-6), soda-lime glass (50 MPa, nu 0.22, E 70 GPa, alpha 9.0e-6) અને fused silica (110 MPa, nu 0.17, E 72 GPa, alpha 0.55e-6) ની thermal shock resistance સરખાવો. કોને પાણીમાં ઠારી શકાય અને કેમ તે કહો.

q.en: A furnace wall is 230 mm of firebrick (k 1.0 W/m K) on the hot side and 115 mm of insulating brick (k 0.12 W/m K) outside it. The hot face is at 1200 C and the cold face at 50 C. Find the heat loss per m2, the interface temperature, and the money saved per m2 in a month if the furnace runs continuously at Rs 8 per kWh.
q.gu: ભઠ્ઠીની દીવાલ ગરમ બાજુ 230 mm firebrick (k 1.0 W/m K) અને બહાર 115 mm insulating brick (k 0.12 W/m K) ની છે. ગરમ સપાટી 1200 C અને ઠંડી સપાટી 50 C છે. પ્રતિ m2 ઉષ્માનો વ્યય, interface નું તાપમાન, અને ભઠ્ઠી સતત ચાલે તો Rs 8 પ્રતિ kWh પર એક મહિનામાં પ્રતિ m2 કેટલા રૂપિયા બચે તે શોધો.

q.en: A firebrick sample of bulk volume 120 cm3 weighs 320 g dry and 345 g after soaking in water. Find its bulk density, its water absorption, its apparent porosity and its true density, and say what that porosity does to the brick.
q.gu: 120 cm3 bulk volume નો firebrick નમૂનો સૂકો 320 g અને પાણીમાં પલાળ્યા પછી 345 g છે. તેની bulk density, water absorption, apparent porosity અને true density શોધો, અને એ porosity ઈંટ સાથે શું કરે તે કહો.

q.en: A bracket is glued to a plate with an epoxy whose lap shear strength is 20 MPa. The overlap is 25 mm wide and 40 mm long and the working load is 5 kN. Find the shear stress in the joint, its factor of safety, and the greatest load it may carry at a required factor of safety of 3.
q.gu: Bracket એક plate પર 20 MPa lap shear strength વાળા epoxy થી ગુંદાય છે. Overlap 25 mm પહોળું અને 40 mm લાંબું છે અને કામનો લોડ 5 kN છે. જોડાણમાં shear stress, તેનું factor of safety, અને 3 નું factor of safety જોઈએ તો વધુમાં વધુ કેટલો લોડ ઉપાડી શકે તે શોધો.

q.en: A bakelite support of dielectric strength 18 kV/mm is used on an 11 kV busbar. For a 3 mm sheet, find the breakdown voltage and the factor of safety at 11 kV; then find the least thickness that gives a factor of safety of 3, and say why the surface path is checked separately.
q.gu: 18 kV/mm dielectric strength વાળું bakelite support 11 kV busbar પર વપરાય છે. 3 mm sheet માટે breakdown વોલ્ટેજ અને 11 kV પર factor of safety શોધો; પછી factor of safety 3 આપતી ઓછામાં ઓછી જાડાઈ શોધો, અને સપાટીનો રસ્તો અલગ કેમ ચકાસાય તે કહો.

learning_outcomes.gu: વિવિધ અધાતુઈ સામગ્રીનું વર્ગીકરણ, ગુણધર્મો અને ઉપયોગ સમજવા.
